assumptions: The Linear webhook payload includes comment.id, comment.body, comment.reactionType, and comment.reactionEmoji fields.
A Slack bot token with channels:write and threads:read scopes is available.
The Slack thread ts (timestamp) is either provided by the webhook or derived from the Linear comment creation timestamp.
The Linear GraphQL API uses a nested mutation structure where reactableId and react are input fields.
Slack message posting requires a channel identifier and a timestamp (ts) to identify the target thread.

example.query: mutation AddReaction($input: ReactionAddInput!) { reactionAdd(input: $input) { success reaction { id } } }

notes: Uses GraphQL mutation reactionAdd with input fields reactableId (comment ID) and react (emoji string).
Requires Bearer token authentication via LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable.
ReactableId corresponds to the comment ID being reacted to.
